title: 165 Effect of supplement type on growing heifers while grazing dormant cool season grasses
content:
Abstract
The number of stocker operations in Southwest Missouri has increased over the past several years. While the impact of type of feed supplement on stocker cattle grazing tall grass native range has been previously evaluated, there is less information on the impact when grazing dormant cool season grasses. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to evaluate the impact of the type of supplementation on animal weight gain while grazing dormant cool season grass pastures from Dec 6, 2022 until Jan 31, 2023. Forty-two head of Hereford heifers were blocked by body weight and assigned to one of three feed supplement treatments, no supplemental feed (CON), Starch (STCH), and Protein (PROT). Heifers in the STCH and PROT treatments were hand fed supplement at 0.75% of initial body weight daily in pens (2 hd/pen). Heifers were assigned to pen based upon weight block (light weight, medium weight, and heavy weight) and treatment for a total of 7 pens/treatment. Heifers were given 45 minutes to eat their feed supplement and any feed refusals were collected, weighed, and subtracted from total feed intake. Heifers in the CON treatment were held in a drylot while the other heifers ate their supplement and then all heifers were moved back to their common pasture. Heifer weights at the start of the study were similar (TRT P = 0.60, Block P < 0.01, Trt x Block = 0.94) with average weights of 238, 241, and 237 kg for STCH, PROT, and CON respectively. Final body weights were statistically different from each other (TRT P < 0.01, Block P < 0.01, and Trt x Block = 0.64) with body weights of 267, 279, and 246 for STCH, PROT, and CON respectively. All three treatments were statistically different from each other (P < 0.05). Average daily gain for the entire study was statistically different across all treatments (TRT P < 0.01, Block P =0.64, and Trt x Block P = 0.69) with estimates of 0.52, 0.68, and 0.15 kg/day for STCH, PROT, and CON respectively. From these results we can conclude that while grazing dormant cool season forage, a supplemental feed high in protein is more effective an increasing weight gain than high starch supplements.
